lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Primitives.Arcsin:QuantumComputation.Specs.arcsin_k25_const_cost
lean.plain: Frozen statement of the 25-bit arcsin cost theorem
lean.annotation: `ArcsinK25ConstCost.json` names both correctness and cost as targets. It allows the candidate to supply `arcsinProgram`, `arcsinAncillas`, and `arcsinK25ConstCost`. Both target statements use the same `arcsinProgram` definition, so the cost bound must hold for the circuit used in the correctness theorem.

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Primitives.Arcsin:QuantumComputation.Specs.arcsin_k25_const_cost
lean.plain: Spacetime bound for the 25-bit arcsin circuit
lean.annotation: The proof rewrites the program to `k25DynCircuit` and the ancilla count to 50. `count_TOFF_k25DynCircuit` supplies the zero-Toffoli conjunct. `count_T_k25DynCircuit` bounds the $T$ count by $3{,}698$, and `hmul` multiplies that bound by $2\cdot25+50$ to give $369{,}800$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.SatisfiesArcsinSpacetimeBound
lean.plain: Zero primitive Toffoli count and a spacetime bound
lean.annotation: For every pair of register arguments of the specified widths, `SatisfiesArcsinSpacetimeBound` requires zero primitive Toffoli gates and bounds the declared width times the primitive $T$ count. The first conjunct prevents a primitive Toffoli from going uncharged in the $T$-only metric. The register disjointness hypothesis belongs to the correctness theorem.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.arcsinK25ConstCost
lean.plain: Numerical bound of 369,800 for the 25-bit circuit
lean.annotation: `arcsinK25ConstCost` is the candidate’s numerical bound, $369{,}800$. The fixed predicate uses it as the right-hand side of a cost inequality. A candidate that supplies a smaller number must prove the same inequality with the smaller bound.

statements.markdown: all target theorem statements and every transitive definition they depend on match the specification
the compiled proof terms depend solely on standard Lean axioms
statements.note: The three permitted axioms are `propext`, `Quot.sound`, and `Classical.choice`. Comparator checks the axiom dependencies of the target proofs, including admitted helpers that introduce `sorryAx`. The reader retains successful local runs for arcsin and Grover Find-Any using the original configurations with sandboxing disabled. Appendix B reports the authors’ separate clean-sandbox procedure.
